notes: NEW: DECISIONS TAB — 'should I, and when?'. WHY: the Scenarios page could plot net-worth curves but could not answer anything, because it conflated two different things. A SCENARIO is an assumed change to the world (a child arrives, a loan closes) — mostly context, not choice. A DECISION is a question being answered, and it must be tested AGAINST that context. Decisions now live on their own page and consume the ENABLED scenarios as their backdrop, which is listed explicitly at the top of the page so it is never ambiguous which world a verdict refers to. WHAT IT ANSWERS: (1) Can I, at this month? (2) When can I — earliest feasible month, plus which constraint blocks it before then and when that lifts. (3) How much — largest workable budget at a given month. The binding constraint shifting over time IS the advice: 'held up by emergency cover until Jul 27, then by EMI vs income' tells you what to fix, not merely that you are stuck. FOUR TESTS, each measured at ITS OWN worst month across the full tenure — not at purchase, not averaged: EMI vs income; EMI vs pre-EMI spare cash; money left over; liquid cash vs an N-month cover floor. THREE APPETITES: Comfortable (15% / 50% / Rs 15,000 / 6mo), Balanced (20% / 62% / Rs 10,000 / 4.5mo), Aggressive (26% / 78% / Rs 5,000 / 3mo). Tightest rule binds. IMPLEMENTATION: no new engine maths. A candidate purchase is expressed as a synthetic house-type scenario and handed to runProjection(), so it inherits salary growth, expense inflation, EMI schedules, investment contributions and every enabled scenario for free. runProjection itself is untouched. THREE MODELLING BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE BUILD: (a) DOWN PAYMENT AS PHANTOM CASHFLOW — the down payment lands as a one-off expense in the purchase month, which cratered that month's surplus and made the cashflow tests fail by roughly the size of the deposit, so no month ever looked affordable. A deposit is a BALANCE-SHEET event: it is now stripped from all three cashflow tests and judged solely by the liquidity test, which asks whether enough cash survives it. (b) AFFORDABILITY SEARCH COLLAPSING TO ZERO — with an absolute down payment held fixed while the price shrank, the cash outlay never fell, so a liquidity failure could never be relieved and the search returned Rs 0 however cheap the item got. The deposit now scales WITH the price (ratio held constant), which is both the intuitive reading of 'how much can I afford' and what makes the binary search monotonic. (c) MEANINGLESS ZERO-PRICE COPY — when no price clears, the page no longer reports 'about Rs 0 works'. It names what is actually binding and what would move it: for a liquidity block, a smaller deposit or more time to build savings, NOT a cheaper purchase. HONESTY NOTE SHOWN IN-APP: the projection books a house or land purchase as money out but does not add the property to assets, so the net-worth cost shown OVERSTATES the true cost by the equity being built. This caveat renders automatically for house and land. A car carries the opposite note — it is consumption and loses value throughout. The page prices a decision; it does not claim to tell you whether to make it. PERFORMANCE: one runProjection is ~20ms over a 14-year horizon. Every search is hard-bounded via DC_LIMITS (sweep 96 months, 6-month stride, 20 coarse probes, 6 fine, 12 bisection iterations) — no loop can run unbounded on any input. Measured: single evaluation ~27ms, full when-can-I sweep ~350ms, affordability search ~190ms. ROBUSTNESS: detail rendering uses a monotonic token rather than a busy flag, so switching decisions mid-run is never dropped and a stale run can never overwrite the panel now on screen. The save path no longer reassigns state.decisions unconditionally, which would have discarded saved decisions if state were ever mid-reload. VERIFIED IN A HEADLESS BROWSER against Hemant's real figures: Punch EV Rs 14.42L, Apr 2027, Comfortable — all four tests clear, tightest is EMI vs income with Rs 20,796 spare, max affordable Rs 24.25L. Affordability is monotonic across appetites (Rs 18.5L / 25.25L / 32.5L with a child in the backdrop). Backdrop confirmed to bite: a kid scenario reduces surplus by exactly Rs 20,000 and shifts decision slack accordingly; disabled scenarios are correctly ignored. Edge cases pass without throwing: zero cost, full-cash purchase, zero tenure, month outside horizon. SCOPE — PURELY ADDITIVE: 541 lines added, 2 replaced (APP_VERSION and the schema-version line). A full byte-diff against v2026.05.05.15 confirms nothing was removed. The Scenarios page is untouched and keeps its existing behaviour, including scenarios defaulting to enabled. Dashboard, Budget, Journal, Projection, Net Worth, Instruments, EMI Calculator, Rates and Edit-my-inputs are unchanged and were re-run clean. The v2026.05.05.15 live-anchored EOM savings fix is untouched. SCHEMA v16: adds state.decisions (array). freshState() now seeds it too, so new users and migrated users both get it. TO VERIFY AFTER DEPLOY: hard-refresh (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R), confirm the console reports v2026.05.06.01, open Decisions from the sidebar, add a purchase and press 'Work it through'. Confirm the Backdrop card lists your enabled scenarios, and that toggling a scenario on the Scenarios page changes the verdict. KNOWN LIMITATION: a house or land purchase is not added to assets by the projection engine, so the 'what saying yes costs' figure is conservative for those. Adding property as a modelled asset is the natural next step and would need its own appreciation assumption.
